sections.label: Global and Singapore economic growth
sections.summary: Global economic resilience and Singapore's own economic strength produced better-than-expected growth of 5% last year.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Last year, the resilience of the global economy, combined with our own economic strength, resulted in better-than-expected growth of 5%.

sections.label: Growth and inflation projections
sections.summary: Growth is projected at 2% to 4%, with inflation at 1% to 2%.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Growth is therefore projected at 2% to 4%; with inflation at 1% to 2%.

sections.label: Budget 2026 first step
sections.summary: Budget 2026 is the first step in the effort to secure Singapore's future in a changed world.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 is the first step in this effort, to secure our future in a changed world.

sections.label: Corporate Income Tax rebate
sections.summary: A 40% Corporate Income Tax rebate in Year of Assessment 2026 gives active companies with a local employee at least $1,500, capped at $30,000.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will support our businesses and help them stay competitive.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will provide a 40% Corporate Income Tax rebate in the Year of Assessment 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Every active company that employed at least one local employee last year will receive a minimum benefit of $1,500.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The total benefit for each company will be capped at $30,000.

sections.label: Growth ambition over next decade
sections.summary: The ambition is to secure growth at the higher end of the 2% to 3% range over the next decade.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our ambition is to secure growth at the higher end of the 2% to 3% range over the next decade.

sections.label: Trade partnerships and agreements
sections.summary: Singapore launched the Future of Investment and Trade Partnership, the EU-Singapore Digital Trade Agreement entered into force, and an Agreement on Trade in Essential Supplies with New Zealand will be signed.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Last year, we launched the Future of Investment and Trade Partnership, bringing together like-minded partners to cooperate in areas like technology, trade facilitation and supply chain resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This month, the EU-Singapore Digital Trade Agreement entered into force – a landmark agreement with robust rules for digital trade.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Later this year, we will sign a first-of-its-kind Agreement on Trade in Essential Supplies with New Zealand – to ensure the continuity of critical trade flows between our two countries in times of crisis.

sections.label: Support for companies internationalising
sections.summary: Enhances grant support levels, expands the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation, and increases maximum loan quantum under the Enterprise Financing Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we will do more to support Singapore companies as they venture abroad.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will enhance the support levels for grant schemes that support companies to internationalise – up to 70% for small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and up to 50% for non-SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Under the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation scheme, companies automatically enjoy a 200% tax deduction for selected qualifying activities, capped at $150,000.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will allow more qualifying activities to be eligible for such automatic tax deduction claims and raise the cap to $400,000.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will enhance the Enterprise Financing Scheme by increasing the maximum loan quantum for trade and fixed asset loans.

sections.label: Research, Innovation and Enterprise investment
sections.summary: Invests $37 billion under the RIE2030 plan, around 1% of GDP each year.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Singapore must be a place where frontier technologies are developed, tested and commercialised.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we will invest $37 billion under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise, or RIE2030 plan.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This reflects our sustained commitment to research and innovation, amounting to around 1% of gross domestic product (GDP) each year.

sections.label: Quantinuum quantum computer in Singapore
sections.summary: Quantinuum has established operations here and will host its latest quantum computer in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Quantinuum, one of the world's leading quantum computer companies, has established operations here and will be hosting its latest quantum computer in Singapore, making us the first country outside America to host this system.

sections.label: Enhancing Startup SG Equity
sections.summary: Sets aside $1 billion to enhance Startup SG Equity and expand its scope to growth-stage companies.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To date, the scheme has focussed mainly on early-stage funding.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will set aside $1 billion to enhance Startup SG Equity, and expand its scope to cover growth-stage companies.

sections.label: Second Anchor Fund tranche
sections.summary: Launches a second $1.5 billion tranche of the Anchor Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We had earlier set up the Anchor Fund to attract and anchor high-quality listings, and we are now seeing encouraging signs of renewed listing activity on the Singapore Exchange (SGX).

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will therefore launch a second $1.5 billion tranche of the Anchor Fund.

sections.label: Financial Sector Development Fund top-up
sections.summary: Expands the programme with a $1.5 billion top-up to the Financial Sector Development Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To build on this momentum, I will expand the programme, with a $1.5 billion top-up to the Financial Sector Development Fund.

sections.label: AI Centres of Excellence
sections.summary: More than 60 firms, including Google and Microsoft, have set up AI Centres of Excellence in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Today, more than 60 firms, including Google and Microsoft, have set up AI Centres of Excellence here.

sections.label: National AI Missions launch
sections.summary: Singapore will launch national AI Missions to drive AI-led transformation in advanced manufacturing, connectivity, finance and healthcare.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We must organise at a national level and move with speed and scale.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will therefore launch a new set of national AI Missions.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These missions will drive AI-led transformation in key sectors of our economy and push the boundaries of what is possible, for Singapore and for the world.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will focus on four sectors: advanced manufacturing, connectivity, finance and healthcare.

sections.label: National AI Council established
sections.summary: A new National AI Council, chaired by the speaker, will provide strategic direction and drive Singapore's AI agenda.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: All this will require a coordinated national effort.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will therefore establish a new National AI Council, which I will chair, to provide strategic direction and to drive Singapore's AI agenda.

sections.label: Champions of AI programme
sections.summary: A new Champions of AI programme will support firms aiming to use AI to comprehensively transform their business.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We want to encourage more to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we will launch a new Champions of AI programme to support firms with the ambition to use AI to comprehensively transform their business.

sections.label: Enterprise Innovation Scheme AI expansion
sections.summary: The Enterprise Innovation Scheme will include AI expenditures as a qualifying activity for Years of Assessment 2027 and 2028, capped at $50,000 each.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will build on the Enterprise Innovation Scheme, which provides businesses with 400% tax deductions on qualifying expenditures in activities like R&D, innovation and capability development.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will expand the scheme to include AI expenditures as a qualifying activity, for the Years of Assessment 2027 and 2028, capped at $50,000 per Year of Assessment.

sections.label: PSG expansion for AI solutions
sections.summary: The PSG will be expanded to support more digital and AI-enabled solutions so every firm can access such tools.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: With support from the PSG, it adopted an AI-enabled restaurant management system to automate ordering and billing, and streamline operations – serving customers faster and growing its revenues in the process.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will expand the PSG to support a wider range of digital and AI-enabled solutions, so that every firm, regardless of size, can access tools that help them work smarter and compete more effectively.

sections.label: AI co-working space and park
sections.summary: A dedicated co-working space serves as a convening hub for the AI community, and a larger AI park will be established at One-North.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It is a dedicated co-working space that serves as a convening hub for our AI community.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will build on this pilot and establish a larger AI park at One-North.

sections.label: AI literacy for IHL students
sections.summary: AI literacy will be strengthened for students across all Institutes of Higher Learning.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For the next generation, we will strengthen AI literacy for students across all our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs).

sections.label: AI training for professions
sections.summary: AI training will start with the accountancy and legal professions and progressively extend to other fields.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Because AI is already reshaping many forms of white-collar and cognitive work, we will start with the accountancy and legal professions, and progressively extend them to other fields.

sections.label: Free premium AI tools access
sections.summary: Singaporeans who take up selected AI training courses will get six months of free access to premium AI tools.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To further encourage learning, we will provide Singaporeans who take up selected AI training courses six months of free access to premium AI tools.

sections.label: Local Qualifying Salary and PWCS changes
sections.summary: The LQS will rise from $1,600 to $1,800, with enhanced and extended PWCS co-funding support and a higher wage increase threshold.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Local Qualifying Salary (LQS) sets the minimum salary that local employees must be paid in firms that hire foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will raise the LQS for full-time local employees from $1,600 to $1,800.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To help businesses defray some of the cost, we will enhance the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme (PWCS).

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will raise the PWCS co-funding support for this year, from 20% to 30%.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will also extend the PWCS for two more years, to 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: From next year, we will raise the minimum wage increase to qualify for PWCS support from $100 to $200.

sections.label: Merging SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore
sections.summary: SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore will merge into a new statutory board jointly overseen by MOE and MOM.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have carefully considered this recommendation and will take a decisive step forward.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will merge SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore into a new statutory board jointly overseen by MOE and MOM.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This new agency will be a one-stop shop for skills training, career guidance and job matching services.

sections.label: Mid-Career Training Allowance extension
sections.summary: From next month, the Mid-Career Training Allowance is extended to part-time training and more industry relevant courses.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: From next month, the Mid-Career Training Allowance will be extended to those who take up not just full-time, but also part-time training.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will also expand coverage to include more industry relevant courses.

sections.label: Senior Employment Credit extension
sections.summary: The Senior Employment Credit will be extended to end-2027 to support employers who continue to employ senior workers.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In the meantime, we will extend the Senior Employment Credit to end-2027, to support employers who continue to employ senior workers.

sections.label: Employment Pass salary increases
sections.summary: From January 2027, EP minimum qualifying salary for new applicants rises to $6,000, and to $6,600 in financial services.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In line with this approach, we will refine and update our foreign worker policies to reflect evolving conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will raise the Employment Pass (EP) minimum qualifying salary for new applicants from $5,600 to $6,000 from January 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For the financial services sector, which has higher salary norms, we will raise the minimum qualifying salary from $6,200 to $6,600.

sections.label: S Pass salary increase
sections.summary: From January 2027, the minimum qualifying salary for new S Pass applicants will be raised from $3,300 to $3,600.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: From January 2027, the minimum qualifying salary for new S Pass applicants will be raised from $3,300 to $3,600.

sections.label: Student Care Fee Assistance threshold
sections.summary: The monthly household income threshold for Student Care Fee Assistance will be raised to $6,500 so more families qualify.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will also strengthen support for student care.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will raise the monthly household income threshold for Student Care Fee Assistance to $6,500, so that more families can qualify.

sections.label: ComLink+ families quarterly payout
sections.summary: A new payout of $500 per quarter will be provided for ComLink+ families who commit to working with family coaches.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, we will provide a new payout of $500 per quarter for all ComLink+ families who make a commitment to work with family coaches and take active steps to make progress.

sections.label: ComLink+ family cash support
sections.summary: A family with two children under ComLink+ can receive around $10,000 per year in cash and CPF top-ups while children are in preschool.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: With these enhancements, a family with two children under ComLink+ can receive around $10,000 per year in cash and Central Provident Fund (CPF) top-ups, while their children are in preschool.

sections.label: CareShield Life premium subsidies
sections.summary: CareShield Life premium subsidies were increased, and $400 million will top up the Long-Term Care Support Fund for the additional subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We also increased CareShield Life premium subsidies to help cushion the impact of the higher premiums.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will top up the Long-Term Care Support Fund by $400 million to fund the additional subsidies.

sections.label: CPF top-up and senior rates
sections.summary: A CPF top-up of up to $1,500 goes to Singaporeans aged 50 and above with savings below the Basic Retirement Sum, and CPF contribution rate increases for senior workers proceed in 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, we will provide a CPF top-up of up to $1,500 for Singaporeans aged 50 and above, and with CPF retirement savings below the Basic Retirement Sum.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, we will proceed with the next step of planned CPF contribution rate increases for senior workers in 2027.

sections.label: CPF extra interest rates
sections.summary: With extra interest, CPF members can earn up to 6% per annum, risk-free, on their CPF balances.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: With the extra interest that CPF offers, CPF members can earn up to 6% per annum, risk-free, on their CPF balances.

sections.label: Low-fee CPF investment scheme
sections.summary: The Government will develop life-cycle investment products under a new scheme for CPF members, requiring low fees and selecting two to three providers.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Currently, such life-cycle investment products are available in the market, but they have traditionally come with high fees.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, rather than leave this entirely to the market, the Government will help shape and develop such products under a new scheme for CPF members.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: A key requirement will be that the fees are kept low.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will select two to three credible providers to keep choices simple for members.

sections.label: Cost-of-Living Special Payment
sections.summary: A Cost-of-Living Special Payment of $200 to $400 in cash goes to eligible Singaporean adults, with higher U-Save rebates for HDB households and $500 in CDC Vouchers in January 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, I will provide a Cost-of-Living Special Payment, comprising $200 to $400 in cash, to Singaporean adults earning up to $100,000 in Assessable Income and who do not own more than one property.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Eligible HDB households will receive 1.5 times the regular amount of U-Save rebates, or up to $570 this financial year.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Third, I will provide another $500 in Community Development Council (CDC) Vouchers   for all Singaporean households in January 2027.

sections.label: Defence spending at 3% GDP
sections.summary: Defence spending is expected to stay at about 3% of GDP, with readiness to spend more if needed.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For now, we expect to keep defence spending at about 3% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But we are prepared to spend more if the need arises.

sections.label: Security-related expenditures to rise
sections.summary: Overall security-related expenditures are expected to rise in coming years to keep Singapore safe in a more complex threat environment.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Taken together, we expect overall security-related expenditures to rise in the coming years to keep Singapore safe and secure in a far more complex threat environment.

sections.label: Carbon tax rate increases
sections.summary: The tax was raised to $45 per tonne for this year and next, with a plan to reach $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The tax has just been raised to $45 per tonne for this year and next, and the plan is to reach $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.

sections.label: Possible lower carbon tax range
sections.summary: If global climate momentum continues to weaken, Singapore may position towards the lower end of the $50 to $80 per tonne range by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If global climate momentum continues to weaken, we may need to position ourselves towards the lower end of the $50 to $80 per tonne range by 2030.

sections.label: Solar deployment target reached early
sections.summary: Singapore's push to expand solar deployment reached its 2030 target of two gigawatt-peak ahead of schedule.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, on clean energy, our sustained push to expand solar deployment is delivering results.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have reached our 2030 solar deployment target of two gigawatt-peak ahead of schedule.

sections.label: Diversifying energy mix and nuclear capabilities
sections.summary: Singapore is pursuing hydrogen, geothermal and civilian nuclear power, building nuclear capabilities, and cooperating with the US and France.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Importantly, we are actively pursuing possibilities to further diversify our energy mix, be it through hydrogen, geothermal energy, or civilian nuclear power.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are building up capabilities in nuclear energy to be able to assess its safety and viability for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have initiated cooperation with the US and France, and are discussing similar arrangements with other partners like South Korea.

sections.label: Sustainable aviation fuel target
sections.summary: Singapore supports sustainable aviation fuel with a target of 1% use for flights departing Singapore this year.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In aviation, we are supporting demand for sustainable aviation fuel, with a target of 1% sustainable fuel use for flights departing Singapore this year.

sections.label: Tax deductions for donations
sections.summary: 250% tax deductions for qualifying donations to IPCs and eligible institutions are extended three years until end-2029.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Today, we provide 250% tax deductions for qualifying donations to Institutions of a Public Character (IPCs) and eligible institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will extend this scheme for another three years until end-2029.

sections.label: Corporate Volunteer Scheme extension
sections.summary: The Corporate Volunteer Scheme, giving 250% tax deductions for employee volunteering or secondment to IPCs, is extended three years until end-2029.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To support these efforts, the Government earlier introduced the Corporate Volunteer Scheme, which provides 250% tax deductions when employees volunteer or are seconded to IPCs.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will extend this Corporate Volunteer Scheme for another three years until end-2029.

sections.label: New SG Partnerships Fund
sections.summary: A new $50 million SG Partnerships Fund will provide differentiated funding tiers, including grants up to $1 million for larger multi-year projects.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At the same time, we have heard feedback on how the fund can be improved, including the need for larger grant amounts, longer funding horizons and broader eligibility.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we will launch a new $50 million SG Partnerships Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is to catalyse ground-up initiatives and help them build sustained capabilities and impact.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The new fund will provide differentiated tiers of funding over different time frames, including grants of up to $1 million for larger, multi-year projects.

sections.label: PARF rebate and tobacco duty
sections.summary: PARF rebate is cut by 45 percentage points and its cap lowered to $30,000, and tobacco excise duty rises 20% from today.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As EVs become more common, the need to encourage early deregistration through the PARF rebate is reduced.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Therefore, I will reduce the PARF rebate by 45 percentage points.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will also lower the PARF rebate cap from $60,000 to $30,000.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Next, to discourage the consumption of tobacco products, I will implement a 20% increase in tobacco excise duty across all tobacco products with effect from today.

sections.label: Investment promotion toolkit update
sections.summary: MTI's expenditure has risen sharply in this Budget to update and strengthen the investment promotion toolkit.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To remain attractive and stay in the game, we must update and strengthen our investment promotion toolkit.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is one reason why MTI's expenditure has risen sharply in this Budget and why it is likely to remain elevated in the years ahead.

sections.label: Budget funds and fiscal footing
sections.summary: The passage states that resources are set aside in funds for future needs, with further top-ups in this Budget, and that spending will be supported by revenues.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We also need to strengthen assurance for families, enhance social mobility and boost retirement adequacy so that Singaporeans can face each stage of life with confidence and peace of mind.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have set aside resources through specific funds for major future needs, including critical infrastructure investments for our energy transition and coastal protection.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In this Budget, we will make further top-ups to the relevant funds to support the development of Changi Airport, as well as our longer-term economic strategies.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Government will manage this increase carefully, ensuring that spending remains supported by revenues and consistent with our objective of maintaining a balanced Budget over the medium term.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In contrast, we begin this term of Government in Singapore on a firm fiscal footing.

sections.label: Parliament approves financial policy question
sections.summary: The Question is that Parliament approves the Government's financial policy for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027, and the debate stands adjourned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That Parliament approves the financial policy of the Government for the Financial Year 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027." In accordance with paragraph (1) of Standing Order No 89, the debate now stands adjourned.
